title: Niche marketing and mass marketing
notes: Authored 2026-10-06 under standard v0.2.0-draft. All claims are provenance generated_gap, verification unverified.

blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Define niche marketing and mass marketing, and weigh the benefits and limitations of each approach against the business's circumstances.

blocks.heading: Two approaches to the whole market
blocks.text: First, the word: a market, as marketers use it, is the customers for a product - the people already buying it and the people who might. Mass marketing sells one product, with one promotion, to the whole of that market, treating every customer alike: one bread loaf, one radio advertisement, one price. Niche marketing instead targets a small, clearly defined group within the market - vegetarian touring cyclists, say - with a product and promotion designed around that group's particular tastes.

blocks.heading: Choosing between them
blocks.text:
Take two firms at the extremes. A Swiss firm mass-markets a simple quartz watch: one design, made in huge quantities, promoted on television to everyone who needs to know the time. The benefits are a wide reach and large total sales from a single product, but its message speaks to everyone at once and to no group exactly, and a cheaper copy can undercut the whole approach. A Namibian jeweller instead designs beaded watchstraps for safari guides - a niche. She meets that group's wants closely and faces few direct rivals, but her group is small, so total sales stay modest and the business depends heavily on it.

The choice therefore depends on how different the customer groups' needs are, how large each group is, and what the business can afford: uniform needs favour the mass approach; sharply different needs and a small budget often point to the niche.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Topic 3.1.2 explained why markets shift and competition sharpens; the niche-or-mass choice is where a business decides which customers it will fight for. Topic 3.1.4 turns that choice into segments with named boundaries, and topic 3.3 supplies the marketing-mix tools for whichever ground is chosen.
